problem: Training VLN/VDN agents with deep RL needs massive data and expensive photo-realistic simulation, and existing RL packages (Dopamine, TF-Agents) target standard Gym/ALE problems rather than compute-heavy multimodal embodied navigation. Per-episode work such as instruction encoding is also duplicated at every step.
motivation: Vision-and-language navigation agents learn cross-modal policies with RL, which pushes data-scaling requirements. Simulation can be fanned out across many actor machines while a central learner trains, so a scalable framework makes more expensive end-to-end training of vision and language modules practical.
key_idea: A lightweight TensorFlow 2 framework built on SEED RL (IMPALA/V-trace) that adds Agent, Environment, Actor, Learner and Problem abstractions, with the agent split into Torso/Neck/Head so per-episode computation is done once and reused.
insight: The Torso/Neck/Head split lets per-trajectory computation (e.g. instruction encoding) run once instead of at every step, which becomes prohibitively expensive as episodes lengthen. Centralizing inference and training in one learner while distributing simulation across actors scales VLN. No ablations or quantitative experiments are reported.
method: Agent (Torso/Neck/Head): tf.keras.Model split into Torso (pre-processing once per trajectory, batched over timesteps), Neck (per-step recurrent logic using Torso output) and Head (post-processing once per trajectory over all steps).

Environment: Gym-like interface with reset/step returning EnvOutput (observation, reward, done, info), encapsulated by the Actor so different policies can roll out in different environment partitions.

Actor: runs the environment and infers actions with the current policy, periodically copying weights from the Learner. Thousands can run in parallel; eval actors send metrics to an aggregator (e.g. Tensorboard).
Learner: dequeues batched trajectories from many actors and trains on GPU/TPU with V-trace off-policy correction, supporting hyperparameter schedules and gradient clipping.
Problem: Python class defining validation metrics, optimizer and losses, e.g. get_episode_loss_type and select_actor_action for mixing policy-gradient and supervised (teacher-forcing) episodes.

R2R case study: RCM agent implemented on VALAN, with a BiLSTM instruction encoder in get_initial_state, a visual LSTM attending over the instruction in neck, and attention over visual scenes in head. Auxiliary-task pretraining is included.

setting.backbone: RCM agent (BiLSTM instruction encoder, LSTM visual encoder with attention, pre-trained CNN features), trained with the framework
setting.training_data: R2R training set (Matterport3D); mix of supervised expert demonstrations and RL rollouts; optional auxiliary-task pretraining
setting.observation: panoramic RGB encoded by a pre-trained CNN, plus instruction tokens and neighboring-node encodings
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph neighbor nodes plus STOP
setting.simulator: Matterport3D (R2R nav graph); Google StreetView for Touchdown

numbers_note: Software framework paper. Validation metrics appear only in a Tensorboard screenshot, and no numeric results are reported.
results: No quantitative results are reported. The paper describes the architecture and shows a Tensorboard dashboard of validation metrics for an RCM agent trained on R2R.
limitations: No benchmark numbers, scalability measurements or speedup comparisons are given to support the claims.
Tied to TensorFlow 2 and the SEED RL architecture; the R2R case covers only the RCM agent with a discrete nav graph.
